source.title: Junior School Curriculum Design: Indigenous Languages, Grade 7
source.notes: Read directly from the local PDF in designs-grade-7/ via the Read tool (no pages param, per standing instruction), full text extracted natively. ISBN 978-9914-43-936-6, First Published 2022, Revised 2024. STRUCTURAL NOTE, same pattern confirmed at Grade 8 and Grade 9: the front-matter 'SUMMARY OF STRANDS AND SUB STRANDS' table presents three generic skill strands (Listening and Speaking / Reading / Writing, each with generic sub-strand categories, totalling 54 lessons) plus a 6-lesson 'Showcasing Concepts and Skills in Indigenous Language (Exhibitions)' entry (60 total) - but the actual body of the document is organised around 9 real-world THEMES (Indigenous Homes, ICT - Internet Access and Use, Safety at Home, Environmental Conservation, Cultural Diversity, The Farm, Talents and Gifts, Indigenous Knowledge: Art, Patriotism), each theme containing exactly one Listening & Speaking sub-strand, one Reading sub-strand, and one Writing sub-strand (2 lessons each, 6 per theme x 9 themes = 54, + 6 lesson Showcasing = 60), with genuinely different content per theme. Following the body's organisation (themes as strands, matching the Grade 8/9 precedent), each Theme is recorded here as a 'strand' with its three L&S/Reading/Writing components as subStrands. Content is generic-English-medium (grammar concepts, listening/reading strategies, essay/letter/dialogue/narrative structure, presentation skills) applied to indigenous-language-medium themes, not actual vocabulary in one specific mother tongue, since KICD's design does not prescribe a single indigenous language among Kenya's 40+. All 9 themes carry genuinely distinct content (not the same theme retold three ways).

scopeNotes: include: the two named worked examples of a request are library membership and club membership — both are explicit, KICD-supplied scenarios

assessmentSignal.listeningAndSpeaking: Rubric's 'Meets expectations' row requires identifying specific information/main ideas from oral texts, transcribing accurately, retelling tongue twisters fluently, recognising how to begin AND end a conversation (not just one), and engaging in a conversation for effective communication (not just reciting memorised lines) — confirming conversational skills are assessed as interactive, not scripted.
assessmentSignal.reading: Rubric requires identifying vocabulary from a written text, responding to BOTH direct and inferential questions (inferential is explicitly a separate, harder bar than direct), summarising information from visuals AND texts, identifying features of a trickster narrative and a fable as two distinct forms, and selecting/reading grade-appropriate materials independently (extensive reading).
assessmentSignal.writing: Rubric requires a coherent AND well-sequenced paragraph (sequencing is a named criterion, not just grammatical correctness), paraphrasing (not copying) information from a text, composing an SMS and a letter of request using correct format/language/organisation as functional-writing genres with real structural conventions, and composing essays/imaginative dialogues/narratives using correct structure — confirming format knowledge (not just content) is explicitly graded.
